      "review_stars": 3.0,
      "review_date": "2022-01-16 06:07:34",
      "review_text": "Unfortunately, we came during the pre-fixed menu. There were no sides and no variety of appetizers. After reading the reviews of the food I was sad to see the menu look so bare and lonely. \nOur server was great, very friendly and the Sommelier was excellent. I chose the mushrooms, the lobster pasta and chocolate mousse. The mushrooms were hearty but the lobster pasta only had about 5 small pieces of lobster. My husband ordered the Ceasar salad, salmon and crème brûlée. He enjoyed his salad but the salmon filet was small.  With 3 (possibly small) \n items per person, you may want to grab an appetizer in the lobby bar before you come. \nIt also took forever to get each course. We were seated at 6:55pm and didn't leave until 9:25pm. My husband and son went back to the room while I waited at the table an additional 15 minutes for 2 cookies and a side of vanilla ice cream. I asked a manager who walked by to check on the dessert and to get me a copy of the itemized receipt. He seemed annoyed. Overall, maybe I'll return when the regular menu is back.."
    },
    {
      "review_stars": 5.0,
      "review_date": "2021-12-22 22:11:03",
      "review_text": "First off, I want to say all of the staff were amazing but we loved our server Autumn. She was so sweet and really knew the menu. We ordered everything she recommended. \n\nWe got a bottle of wine to start, very crisp and light. Then for appetizers we ordered a dozen oysters which came in fresh from Baja, CA. I love that they provided a large amount of lemon, hot sauce and this amazing house made sauce. I could have eaten 100. One of the best selection of oysters we had. The quail and side salad was phenomenal. Just watch out for the little bones.\n\nFor dinner, I got the halibut which was so rich and tender I could barely scoop it up. It was very flavorful. Bae got the filet and potatoes which was cooked to perfection. We got a side of the cauliflower and it was the perfect side. \n\nWe opted for the chocolate mousse cake since chocolate is my favorite but to be honest wouldn't recommend. I wish they would expand their dessert menu but overall great night sitting by the water!"
    },
    {
      "review_stars": 4.0,
      "review_date": "2021-12-10 20:06:30",
      "review_text": "Had a great time! Good service, drinks and food. Very knowledgeable. The filet mignon was amazing and finally found a place with a good bearnaise. Lots of tarragon and saffron on the menu. Would be 5 stars with a smidge lower price tag. The lighting was a little \"shoe storey\" but maybe because we were seated in the middle of the room. We also got wine recs starting close to $300. Apart from that a great experience."
    }
  ]
}

    {
      "review_stars": 5.0,
      "review_date": "2021-08-11 23:42:10",
      "review_text": "I know, I know.... People might be shocked to see that O'Malley's gets a five star rating from me. I would describe it as a \"neighborhood bar located at ground zero of tourist central\".  Some would call it a dive bar, it isn't.   I am a bit of a dive bar connoisseur and O'Malley's falls short or more accurately elevates above the standard of dive bar.   Mostly for the lack of bar flys sitting at the counter at 11:00am.  \n\nThey have an amazing team, many who have worked here for years and are loved by SB locals.   Duane and Katie are fabulous and today as I write this Haley is working!   She just made me an amazing margarita.  \n\nNow, why five stars? Because I come here so freakin' much.   How could I ever knock off a star for a place I frequent many times in a month.  SB falls short in the sports bar department and O'Malleys has TV's in abundance!  Inside, on the patio and now out front on State Street.   Whether you love football, Dodger games or European Soccer they have it on.   If you are visiting SB you might have noticed it is not uncommon to pay $16 for a drink, not O'Malley's, I don't know how many times I got my bill and said \"we ordered five drinks\" and heard them respond \"yes, they are all on there\".  As a tourist you might find O'Malley's to be a little unkept for the fancy SB vibe you are used to, but come back on your next visit, and then your next.   I'm sure you will embrace it as I do."

}

      "review_date": "2021-12-24 17:06:33",
      "review_text": "One of the best restaurants and Mediterranean food I've ever had!! They are very clean and the employees there are very nice and good energy as well as the owner.. I'm definitely going back. DEFINITELY RECOMMEND!!"
    },
    {
      "review_stars": 5.0,
      "review_date": "2021-12-24 16:31:23",
      "review_text": "Honestly i cant describe this place. It is one of my favorite stops in SB. The shawarma Sandwich taste sooo good and the hummus is the best. Alo the fried chicken was something else. Crispy and Halal. The staff are so friendly and the vibes are super. Will definitely come back. This place is super awesome."
    },
    {
      "review_stars": 1.0,
      "review_date": "2021-12-24 15:02:14",
      "review_text": "We were excited to try this place out, but we're extremely disappointed. The service was slow, it seemed like there were only two people working. The silverware was not very clean. The ambiance was awkward, very quiet, like a doctors office lobby. The beef schwarma sandwich was not good at all. The meat had no flavor, couldn't taste any seasonings. It was also wrapped in a tortilla. A tortilla??! While the menu says \"flat bread.\" I was hoping that at least the baklava would be good, but it was so dry. The hummus that came with the schwarma wasn't that great, either. The Turkish coffee was decent though. Would not recommend and will not come back. 1 star for being ambitious enough to open a new restaurant in town."
    }
  ]
}

CLAIM: Mr B Restaurant & Cafe is a Middle Eastern restaurant and cafe.

      "review_date": "2021-10-16 04:22:16",
      "review_text": "i've been really craving thai food and i've not have thai food in santa barbara. however, everything here is kind of subpar to me sadly (i say this as in i have had better) in a way, everything here is weirdly healthy??? still, i think they have a decent pad thai! their pineapple fried rice was just kind of plain and looks a little sad and not colorful. to be real idk how this stuff is cooked \"authentically\" but there's just something off about it. the egg roll was good, just a good ol egg roll. and their papaya salad was also okay! their curry was also okay i think everything was okay and i'm not mad at it just a little sad\ntheir service is good! the ladies are super cute and they r the reason why i would go back"

      "review_date": "2021-10-12 15:54:31",
      "review_text": "Excellent food great service. I'm found this place on a whim and so glad I did!\nGo here get the curry and make sure you're able to get a Thai iced tea!\n\nI love a pad thai, but so many places make them so heavy, this was crisp and bright flavored- so good."

      "review_stars": 5.0,

    {
      "review_stars": 5.0,
      "review_date": "2017-12-09 00:49:10",
      "review_text": "We loved this place! We stayed at the hotel for a couple of days and had most of our meals here. The staff was great as well as the owner who is really a great guy. I don't understand the negative reviews but I guess that happens time to time."
    },
    {
      "review_stars": 2.0,
      "review_date": "2015-01-05 17:58:01",
      "review_text": "This place is really convenient if you're staying at the hotel in the same parking area. I ordered the ribeye and I gotta say the flavor is underwhelming  I guess I expected too much in that it would be steakhouse quality but it's not.  It's more like average coffee shop quality so I'm not impressed. The flavor also was lacking a bit as it's not seasoned all that well."
    },
    {
      "review_stars": 1.0,
      "review_date": "2014-11-28 21:48:31",
      "review_text": "I'm not sure how this place is getting good reviews. I'm staying at the hotel because my daughter is hospitalized at cottage. Having to spend Thanksgiving in the hospital really bites but we were with family. My husband didn't want to eat the hospital food so suggested the restaurant. They had a special menu as it was Thanksgiving. I ordered it to go to eat dinner with our daughter. When I got it back to the hospital room I couldn't be more disappointed. $20 plate of barely any food. I let my husband eat mine and I had what the hospital served which was half the price double the food and better quality. I mean there were literally 4 green beans and 3 carrot slices in each container. We will not be eating here ever again. What a rip off."
    }
  ]
}

CLAIM: The restaurant takes reservations.

Verdict:

      "review_stars": 1.0,
      "review_date": "2021-12-12 04:20:43",
      "review_text": "Husband and I walked by Petit Valentien this afternoon and the Ethiopian lunch dishes we saw on the patio looked great, so we stopped in for dinner about 30 minutes ago. We weren't in a huge rush, but we didn't have hours to dine, because I had dough proofing at home and needed to attend to it. Hubby walked in and checked in with waitress and came out saying we should take any seat we wanted and she'd be right out with menus. So, we sat next to the Xmas tree on the patio and waited... and waited... and waited.\n\nWe figured she couldn't see us so we moved right next to the front door, where she couldn't miss us. After waiting several minutes, I decided we would wait 5 more minutes and then find somewhere else for dinner. After 3 minutes, a 30-something brunette waitress came and dropped off menus. I let her know the table was wobbly and she said she'd bring a block for it (which she never did). Oddly, I detected a twinge of attitude from the waitress with that exchange... not sure why, but there was an element of nastiness in her tone. She also turned on the table-side heater, which was very effective, if somewhat atmosphere-killing, because of its very bright coils.\n\nI pulled up Yelp to look at the pics of the entrees and we settled on what we wanted to order. After about 5 more minutes, the waitress returned and informed us that dinner would take longer here than other restaurants. I let her know I was proofing dough at home and if we ordered immediately, how long would it take. She replied that if we ordered faster, the food would come faster. (Duh! Crazy how that works!) Again, a twinge of nastiness.\n\nHubby and I heard the specials and I asked her to repeat the sides on one of the specials. Attitude was ramping up from her. Which is great to be able to order a balanced meal. \n\nOverall, I'm still scared of the big aggressive dogs that come here but with a little bit of exposure therapy, I can see putting this place into my lunchtime rotation. \n\nThe food is pretty fresh and tasty. The food is affordable. It was worth the wait and....possibly worth the exposure to scary dogs."

**No, juice fasts do not “detoxify” the body in the way most people think.**  
The liver, kidneys, lungs, skin, and gut already perform sophisticated detoxification processes. A short‑term juice fast may give you a temporary “clean‑up” feeling, but it does not remove toxins that are already stored in fat or that are produced by normal metabolism. In some cases, a juice fast can even be harmful, especially if it lasts more than a few days or is repeated frequently.

---

## 1. What “detox” really means

| Organ | Primary detox functions | What it actually does |
|-------|------------------------|-----------------------|
| **Liver** | Phase I (oxidation, reduction, hydrolysis) → Phase II (conjugation) → excretion | Breaks down drugs, alcohol, metabolic waste, and some environmental toxins; produces bile to help eliminate fat‑soluble substances. |
| **Kidneys** | Filtration of blood → excretion of water‑soluble waste (urea, creatinine, drugs) | Remove nitrogenous waste and excess electrolytes. |
| **Lungs** | Expel CO₂ and volatile substances | Remove carbon dioxide and some alcohols. |
| **Skin** | Sweat → excretion of salts, urea, some toxins | Minor route for water‑soluble waste. |
| **Gut** | Bacterial metabolism, bile excretion, fecal elimination | Remove indigestible food, some toxins, and bacterial by‑products. |

These organs work continuously, 24/7, and are highly efficient. They do not need “detox diets” to function.

---

## 2. What a juice fast actually does

1. **Caloric restriction** – You consume very few calories (often <200–400 kcal/day).  
2. **High carbohydrate intake** – Mostly simple sugars from fruit and some complex carbs from vegetables.  
3. **Low protein & fat** – Minimal amino acids and fatty acids.
